security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are documentation, tests, fixed imports, status constants, or expected local file operations. Confirmed risks include CAPTCHA circumvention, unrestricted authenticated fetching, arbitrary credential forwarding, command-line secret exposure, and unbounded direct downloads. No prompt injection text was found. Static review was capped at 400/766 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 366 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The skill automatically attempts CAPTCHA and anti-bot challenges.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automated challenge solving and require user handoff whenever a CAPTCHA or bot verification appears.

remediation.issue: Stored IEEE API keys can be appended to any configured endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and validate the endpoint against documented IEEE hostnames before attaching credentials.

remediation.issue: Direct and browser downloads accept unrestricted URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only HTTP and HTTPS, reject credentials in URLs, and block private, loopback, link-local, and file destinations.

remediation.issue: Sensitive values can be provided through command-line options.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secret-bearing arguments and accept keys or tokens only through hidden input, standard input, or a platform secret store.

remediation.issue: Direct responses are fully buffered without a size limit.
remediation.suggestion: Stream responses to temporary files and enforce Content-Length and incremental byte limits before replacement.

remediation.issue: Browser-control requests can target an arbitrary proxy.
remediation.suggestion: Default to loopback, reject remote proxy hosts unless explicitly trusted, and require authenticated encrypted transport for remote use.

semantic_findings.title: Automated CAPTCHA Circumvention
semantic_findings.description: The skill detects CAPTCHA gaps and simulates human-like drags or checkbox clicks to defeat provider verification controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation explicitly calculates CAPTCHA gaps, generates human-like movement, retries alternate profiles, and checks whether verification passed.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Forwarded to Arbitrary Endpoint
semantic_findings.description: A configured IEEE endpoint accepts any URL, and the downloader appends the stored API key before sending the request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint is stored without hostname validation, then converted to a URL and receives the API key as a query parameter.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Authenticated URL Fetching
semantic_findings.description: User-supplied URLs are fetched directly or inside an authenticated browser without scheme, hostname, or private-network restrictions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI accepts arbitrary URL strings and passes them to fetch or browser navigation without an allowlist or private-address check.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Direct Download Buffering
semantic_findings.description: Direct downloads buffer the entire response in memory before validation and writing, with no byte limit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The response arrayBuffer is fully materialized before content checks, and this path has no Content-Length or streamed byte cap.

semantic_findings.title: Command-Line Secret Exposure
semantic_findings.description: API keys and institutional tokens can be passed as command arguments, exposing them through shell history and process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser defines API-key, insttoken, and authtoken arguments, and cmd_set stores those argument values as credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted CDP Proxy Destination
semantic_findings.description: The CLI accepts any proxy URL and sends browser-control payloads to it without requiring loopback or explicit trust.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The proxy argument is only trimmed, then receives target identifiers, URLs, selectors, and generated browser JavaScript through HTTP requests.

content.value_statement: Finding authorized full text across publishers, repositories, and institutional portals is slow. This skill routes requests and verifies downloaded academic files.
actual_capabilities: Routes Chinese literature to CNKI and English literature through publisher, open-access, or institutional routes.
Downloads PDF, HTML, XML, CAJ, and requested supporting information when the selected source provides them.
Uses Elsevier, Springer Nature, and IEEE credentials from a local configuration file.
Reuses an authenticated Chrome session through a CDP proxy for authorized institutional access.
Verifies file signatures, content types, hashes, and download status in a manifest.
Resolves metadata through Crossref, Europe PMC, Unpaywall, and arXiv.
limitations: Institutional routes require the user to authenticate in Chrome and enable remote debugging.
Publisher API keys do not guarantee full-text entitlement.
The skill cannot lawfully bypass paywalls, DRM, two-factor authentication, or missing subscriptions.
Automatic verification controls may violate provider terms and should be disabled before use.

use_cases.description: Download one article by DOI or exact title and verify the resulting file.

use_cases.title: Collect a Reading List
use_cases.description: Process a confirmed DOI list and record each article's route, status, and integrity details.

use_cases.title: Access Chinese Literature

prompt_templates.title: Download One Paper
prompt_templates.prompt: Download the article with DOI [DOI]. Do not download supporting information. Save it in [folder] and report the verified format.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one DOI and wants the main article.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Open Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a lawful open-access copy of [title]. Download the main article only and explain which source provided it.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has a title but no publisher access.

prompt_templates.title: Process a DOI List
prompt_templates.prompt: Process these confirmed DOIs: [list]. Ask once about supporting information, use lawful routes, and summarize every result.
prompt_templates.scenario: A research assistant needs a traceable batch download.

prompt_templates.title: Use Institutional Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authenticated Chrome session for [articles]. Stop for identity checks, avoid automatic CAPTCHA solving, and produce a verified manifest.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user has authorized library access and browser control.

output_examples.output: The article was downloaded from an open-access repository. The PDF signature and checksum were verified, and the manifest records the source.

output_examples.input: Retrieve three confirmed articles through my library and include supporting information.
output: Two main PDFs were downloaded through authorized routes.
One article requires user authentication before retrying.
Supporting information was found for one completed article.

output_examples.input: Find an open copy of an exact article title.
output_examples.output: No lawful open copy was confirmed. The result records the attempted repositories and does not claim a successful download.

best_practices: Provide exact titles, DOIs, or a confirmed paper list before starting downloads.
Use hidden input or standard input for API keys, and review the destination folder first.
Confirm supporting-information preferences once, then inspect the manifest and downloaded file signatures.
anti_patterns: Do not request unlimited topic downloads or entire journal issues.
Do not paste institutional passwords, session tokens, cookies, or one-time codes into chat.
Do not use automated CAPTCHA solving or access content beyond the user's authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill bypass paywalls?
faq.answer: No. It uses lawful open-access sources, configured publisher APIs, or the user's authorized institutional access.

faq.question: Which identifiers can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide DOIs, exact titles, PMIDs, article URLs, or a confirmed list.

faq.question: Where are publisher credentials stored?
faq.answer: They are stored locally in the configured credentials file with restricted permissions.

faq.question: Can it download supporting information?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires an explicit supporting-information choice before creating download output.

faq.question: Why is Chrome remote debugging required?
faq.answer: Institutional routes need access to the browser session where the user already authenticated.

faq.question: What happens when access fails?
faq.answer: The skill records a typed failure, preserves attempted routes, and identifies any required user action.
